pakṣa
(‘that which is accepted’)
------------------------------------------
This word is used in several senses. A period of a fortnight between a new-मोओन् day and a full-मोओन् day is called ‘pakṣa’. That which ends in the former is called kṛṣṇapakṣa and in the latter, śuklapakṣa.
In लोगिच्, the word indicates the minor term like the hill from which smoke is being emitted. (See ANUMĀNA and also NYĀYADARŚANA.)
In philosophical disputations it indicates a view logically presented. For e.g., पूर्वपक्ष (prima facie view) and uttarapakṣa (final view).
In वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, it indicates the two rectangular aisles or sides of an altar, to the north and the south.
